parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM .mjs output requirement, manual CLI parsing, local-only modules, schedule/job output compatibility, and executable-based black-box observation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode being injected, the agent chose a single-owner path: probe behavior, write argparse/job/schedule/test12 modules itself, then verify.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a compact four-file solution with lib/argparse.mjs, lib/job.mjs, lib/schedule.mjs after renaming scheduler.mjs, and test12.mjs importing local .mjs modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the local schedule module into test12.mjs, placed all required files under /output, and delivered a final response listing the structure and verification results.
parallel.verification: Ran executable probes, compared normal outputs, read completed error/help background results, investigated degenerate timeout/overflow inputs, and confirmed --a= form equality.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official defect remained; the final response noted intentional non-replication of degenerate hanging/overflow inputs, but official evaluation passed all cases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argument parsing, local-only import, schedule representation, and exact output requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-agent iterative plan with broader black-box probes, initial module creation, parser debugging, and repeated local validation without delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented a five-file solution: test12.mjs plus argument_parser.mjs, python_int.mjs, python_repr.mjs, and scheduler.mjs, adding compatibility layers for integer parsing and error repr.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Kept all generated files under /output, wired test12.mjs to the local modules with explicit .mjs imports, and delivered the module hierarchy in the final response.
serial.verification: Byte-diffed normal, equals-form, reordered duplicate, signed/padded, Unicode digit, help, and parser-error cases, then ran node --check across all .mjs files.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official defect remained; earlier parser mismatches such as --he help abbreviation were fixed before final validation and official evaluation passed all cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required pure ESM, .mjs, manual CLI parsing, local-module, no external dependency, and output-matching obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations and probed additional argparse and Unicode integer edge cases beyond the core prompt examples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the official outcome; serial explored more edge cases, while parallel implemented enough compatible behavior to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel was launched with swarm mode but used one main actor and no delegation; that actor owned probing, implementation, integration, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial was also one main actor, with no delegation or subagents, and owned every phase directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The nominal parallel run did not produce a child-agent ownership structure, so there is no multi-agent ownership difference to map to the taxonomy.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used local module interfaces between argparse, job, schedule, and test12, including a rename from scheduler.mjs to schedule.mjs to match imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local interfaces between parser, integer parsing, repr, scheduler, and entry modules, revising parser behavior after observed mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both kept interfaces within one actor; no child brief, child return, or cross-agent contract existed, and both integrated local modules successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a lean implementation: custom argparse, Job representation, schedule module, and entry script, then fixed the schedule module filename.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a more elaborate implementation with Python integer and repr compatibility modules, then iteratively patched help-option and parsing behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial invested more in parser edge compatibility, while parallel used a smaller implementation; both produced behavior sufficient for the official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved the completed error/help background result, stopped a stuck probe, retested the problematic executable behavior with explicit timeouts, and closed after equality checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial stopped an early hanging executable probe, continued local investigation, fixed mismatches, and finished after final validation commands succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both managed local tool-result lifecycle adequately; neither had delegated child results to join or missing verifier returns.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel made sequential writes in /output and corrected a filename mismatch by moving scheduler.mjs to schedule.mjs before testing the entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote sequential /output files and patched argument_parser.mjs and python_int.mjs after reading current file state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had single-actor shared-state provenance; no concurrent write collision, overwrite by another agent, or leaked artifact was evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel compared executable and Node outputs for normal cases, error/help paths, and equals-form arguments; official evaluation passed 150/150.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a larger validation suite including node --check and multiple byte-diff cases; official evaluation also passed 150/150.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader self-verification, but the official acceptance result is equal, so no outcome-discordant verification difference exists.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in 1247.76 agent seconds without timeout and closed after final checks despite time spent on degenerate hanging executable probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1129.008 agent seconds without timeout after a longer sequence of local probes and parser fixes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed within the official budget and passed; the parallel run had no fan-out budget pressure because no fan-out happened.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both runs passed 150 of 150 tests, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. The parallel-labeled run entered swarm mode but did not execute child agents or any multi-agent delegation; it solved the task as a single actor with a compact four-file ESM implementation. The serial run also solved the task as a single actor, using a broader compatibility-focused implementation and more edge-case validation. The concrete task-solving difference is implementation style and verification breadth, not success or failure.
parallel_contributors: Direct single-actor probing and file creation produced the required ESM .mjs artifact.
Representative executable comparisons and error/help checks supported closure before official evaluation.
serial_contributors: Broader single-agent probing found parser abbreviation and integer-representation details before final closure.
Final syntax checks and byte diffs across multiple argument cases supported the same passing official result.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used argparse/job/schedule modules and acknowledged degenerate nonpositive-input divergence in its final response.
Serial added python_int and python_repr helpers and fixed parser behavior through multiple local edits before passing.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; no retained parallel coordination pattern because no executed child-agent or multi-agent boundary occurred
